faq.metaTitle: faq: pricing, data protection and setup · maskera
faq.metaDescription: Answers to common questions about Maskera: is text sent anywhere, is an agreement needed, what it costs, which AI services and browsers work and how to roll it out.
faq.title: FAQ
faq.lede: Short answers to what we are asked most. If your answer is missing, email hej@maskera.dev.

items.q: Is my text sent to Maskera?
items.a: No. Masking runs locally in the browser, in the extension or in your own Node process. Maskera never receives the text or the key that restores it.

items.q: Do we need a data processing agreement?
items.a: Not for the text, because Maskera never receives it. Account and payment details in the customer portal are handled by Hägvall Labs AB under the extension privacy policy.

items.q: Where is the key that restores the text?
items.a: Only on your device. In the extension it lives in the browser's session storage and is cleared when the tab or the browser closes.

items.q: Does Maskera store anything about me?
items.a: maskera.dev counts page views anonymously without cookies. The customer portal stores account and payment details for people who buy Pro or Team. The text you mask is never stored by us.
It can happen, especially with unusual names or noisy scanned text. Review it yourself when a mistake would matter, and report misses so they become test cases. The numbers are on the accuracy page.

items.q: Which AI services does the extension work with?
items.a: ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Copilot, Perplexity and Mistral, plus internal AI sites you turn on yourself.
Chrome, Edge and Firefox on desktop. Safari is coming later. Until the stores open, you can install the extension manually in Chrome and Edge.
Masking itself needs no network. The AI model is downloaded once when you start and is then kept on the device.

items.q: Does it work in languages other than Swedish?
items.a: Maskera is built for Swedish text. Rules such as email and card numbers work in any language, but the model is trained for Swedish names and places.
Yes. The local proxy masks what you type in the chat, the MCP server masks files the agent reads, and guard stops prompts with personal data. See the guides for Claude, Codex and Cursor.

Free gives unlimited rules and 20 AI redactions a month. Pro costs SEK 149 per user and month including VAT, with 7 days free. Team costs SEK 249 per user and month excluding VAT, from 5 users. The agent tools and npm packages are free and open source.

items.q: What is the difference between Pro and Team?
items.a: Pro is for one person: unlimited AI redaction and your own protected words. Team adds a shared word list for the whole organisation, central deployment and rollout support.
Cancel in the customer portal before the next charge. There is no lock-in.
Yes, Team can be paid by annual invoice. Email hej@maskera.dev and we will send one.

items.q: How do we roll the extension out to the whole organisation?
items.a: With Team you deploy the extension in Chrome and Edge through Intune, Jamf or Google Workspace, together with the licence and the shared word list. We send a ready-made template.

guides.metaTitle: guides: connect maskera to claude, codex and cursor · maskera
guides.metaDescription: Step by step: connect Maskera's local proxy or MCP server in Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Codex and Cursor, and test with made-up data.
guides.title: Guides
guides.lede: Step by step for the most common AI tools. The proxy masks what you type in the chat. The MCP server masks files the agent reads.

sections.title: Claude Desktop
sections.body: Start the proxy and keep it running. Then choose Help → Troubleshooting → Enable Developer Mode, followed by Developer → Configure Third-Party Inference…. Enter the base URL http://127.0.0.1:8787 without /v1, your Anthropic API key and the x-api-key auth scheme. Click Apply Changes and then Save & Restart.
sections.note: The exact field names, and how to switch back to your Claude account, are in the client guide.

sections.title: Claude Code
sections.body: With the proxy, everything Claude Code sends is masked, tool results included. With MCP, Claude reads your files through Maskera instead.
sections.code:
# Proxy
npx -y @maskera/mcp proxy
ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8787 claude

# Or the MCP server for files
claude mcp add maskera -- npx -y @maskera/mcp --root .

sections.title: Codex
sections.body: With an API key, Codex goes through the proxy. Signed in with ChatGPT, Codex requires HTTPS, so the local proxy does not work. Use the MCP server instead.
sections.code:
# With an API key
npx -y @maskera/mcp proxy
OPENAI_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8787/v1 codex

# Signed in with ChatGPT: MCP server
codex mcp add maskera -- npx -y @maskera/mcp --root .

sections.title: Cursor
sections.body: Add the MCP server to the project's .cursor/mcp.json. The agent then reads sensitive files with maskera_read_file and writes back with maskera_write_file.

sections.title: Test before you use real data
sections.body: Open the local inspector and send a made-up address. The inspector should show [EPOST_1] going out, and the reply should show the address again.
sections.code:
# The inspector
open http://127.0.0.1:8787/_maskera

# Type in the chat
Skriv ett kort mejl till provnamn.maskera@example.com och bekräfta mötet.

coverage.heading: What is masked?
coverage.servicesLink: All three use the same Swedish model and rules.
coverage.lede: The complete maskera npm package and the browser extension combine fixed rules with the Swedish AI model. Their default choices differ as shown below.

groups.title: AI model: free text
groups.description: Found from context. Accurate on everyday Swedish, though unusual names or phrasing can still slip through.

groups.title: Beyond the npm defaults
groups.description: Additions beyond the npm package defaults, explained in the notes below.

groups.title: Rules: fixed formats
groups.description: Found with fixed format rules. Swedish personal identity numbers are masked even if the check digit is mistyped, as long as the date shape is valid. Web links are caught when they start with http, https or www.

notes.title: Vehicle registration numbers
notes.text: The ready-made rule is enabled in the demo. It is optional in the npm package defaults because the same format can also be a booking or case number.

notes.title: Custom formats
notes.text: Customer, order, invoice and case numbers can be added as custom rules when the organisation's formats are known.

notes.title: Not included automatically
notes.text: Maskera does not classify all sensitive information. Dates, ages, usernames, diagnoses and other sensitive facts are not masked merely because the content is sensitive. Phone numbers written as words are not detected by the numeric rules either.

accuracy.comparisonSummary: Maskera hides the most names, lowercase ones included, and the most addresses. Presidio hides more places and hits far fewer sentences without personal data. Its spaCy model is trained on SUC 3.0, one of the tests, which gives it an advantage there.

tests.name: SUC 3.0, National Library of Sweden
tests.body: The test part of a manually annotated Swedish corpus: newspaper text, fiction and government text. People, places and organisations, in normal text and in lowercase.

tests.name: SIC2, Språkbanken Text
tests.body: 809 manually annotated sentences from Swedish blogs. Informal everyday Swedish with people, places and organisations, plus sentences without personal data.

tests.name: MultiCoNER v2, Swedish
tests.body: Short sentences from Swedish Wikipedia, all lowercase. Only person names count: places and organisations are labelled too loosely, with common words such as "ort" and "flygplats".

tests.name: ai4privacy openpii, Swedish
tests.body: Synthetic Swedish text from another company. Names, street addresses, postcodes, towns and email count. Phone, card and personal identity numbers do not count here, because many of the values are not valid Swedish formats.

accuracy.contextBody: Personal identity numbers are easy to find with ordinary rules. The hard part of Swedish text is words that can be both names and ordinary words or diagnoses.

contextExamples.result: Masks the name Bo and town Boden, while leaving the verb bo (live) untouched.

contextExamples.input: Liv har bott hela sitt liv i Uppsala.
contextExamples.result: Masks the name Liv and Uppsala, while leaving the noun liv (life) untouched.

contextExamples.input: Patienten har Parkinsons sjukdom, men Kalle Parkinson ringde.
contextExamples.result: Masks the person Kalle Parkinson, while leaving the diagnosis Parkinsons sjukdom untouched.

accuracy.contextDemoCta: Try the example in the demo
limits: None of the test texts are in Maskera's training, which uses only generated text. The base model KB-BERT was pretrained by the National Library of Sweden on broad Swedish text and may have seen the same source texts, but never the labels.
Maskera hits words in about one in five sentences without personal data. That is the price of finding lowercase and unusual names, and it means some ordinary words are swapped out needlessly.

Personal identity numbers, organisation numbers, bankgiro and IBAN have no independent Swedish test text. They are found with format rules and check digits and are covered by the project's own tests on GitHub, but are not reported here.
No automatic masking is error-free. Review the text yourself when a mistake could have serious consequences.
accuracy.provenance: Measured on CPU on 2026-11-26: Maskera v20 (q4), Presidio 2.2.366 with sv_core_news_lg 3.8.0, swedish-pii 1.2.0 and OpenAI Privacy Filter (q4 ONNX). The test texts are fetched from Hugging Face and Språkbanken Text when the test runs. Scripts and checksums are on GitHub.

security.metaTitle: security: network requests and model integrity · maskera
security.metaDescription: Maskera's security boundaries, network requests, pinned model artefacts, safe restoration and private vulnerability reporting.
security.title: Security in maskera
security.lede: All masking runs locally on your device. Here is how data moves, how model files are verified and how to report a vulnerability.
dataFlow: Your text and restoration key are never sent to Maskera. The rule layer has no network dependencies and the AI model runs locally in the browser or your own Node process.
On first use, the npm package downloads the AI model (43 MB) once as a regular static file and caches it locally. You can also host the model files on your own server with no external requests.
artifacts: Every npm release is pinned to an exact model version on Hugging Face, so weights cannot change quietly without a new package release.
The build checks every model file with SHA-256. An unexpected or corrupted file stops the build instead of being used silently.
restore: The key contains the original values and must be treated as personal data. Do not log it or store it beside the masked text.

restore() inserts real values wherever placeholder tokens occur. Do not restore untrusted output that will then be fetched as a URL, rendered as HTML or written to logs. Masking protects what is sent; restoration does not sanitise what comes back.
A placeholder already present in the input is never allocated again. Planting [PERSONNUMMER_1] in the source text therefore cannot capture a real value.
security.scopeIntro: Report privately if you find, for example:
inScope: original values or the restoration key leaking to the network, storage or logs contrary to the documented local processing
unexpected network requests beyond the documented one-time downloads of the model and runtime
XSS or injection in the demo at maskera.dev
an exploitable supply-chain risk in the npm packages or model artefacts
an intentional construction that hides personal data from the detectors while a person or language model can still read it
security.qualityBody: A model missing an unusual name or a rule lacking an edge case is normally a quality issue, not a vulnerability. Report such examples publicly so they can become regression cases. A reproducible intentional bypass, however, belongs in a private security report.
security.reportBody: Do not open a public issue for a possible security flaw. Use GitHub's private vulnerability reporting. Only the latest published versions of maskera and @maskera/core receive security fixes, so update before reporting.
security.productionBody: The production guide covers secure integration, fallback to rules, logging, self-hosting, domain-specific test corpora and the production checklist.
security.extensionBody: This page covers the npm packages and open demo. The browser extension's local data handling and licence model are documented in the customer portal.

transparency.metaTitle: privacy & transparency: what leaves the device · maskera
transparency.metaDescription: See what Maskera does, what leaves the device, how the Swedish AI model was trained and which personal data it can miss.
transparency.title: Privacy & transparency
transparency.lede: See what Maskera does, what leaves the device, how the model was trained and what it can miss.
how: You write: “Bo Ek bor i Boden.” Maskera finds the name and the place.
Before the text is sent, they are swapped for placeholders: “[NAMN_1] bor i [PLATS_1].” That is all the AI service sees.
The AI service replies with the same placeholders. Maskera swaps them back on your device, using a key that never leaves it.

Two things find the data. Rules catch fixed formats such as personal identity numbers, phone numbers and email. A small Swedish AI model catches names, places, organisations and addresses in ordinary text. Both run in the browser or in your own Node process.
data: All masking runs locally on your device (browser, extension or your own Node process). Text and restoration keys are never sent to Maskera.
The site's own analytics and hosting are described in the privacy policy. Text entered in the tool is never included.
The rule layer has no network dependencies. The npm package downloads the model and runtime once as static files and can be self-hosted (details on the security page).
limits: Maskera is evaluated openly. The figures, method and caveats are available on the accuracy page.
Known weak points include table-like dumps, OCR noise and data written as words, such as ‘zero seven zero’. Capital letters, misspellings and messy number formats are, however, included in the tests.
Masking is an additional protection layer, not a guarantee. Names and places are found probabilistically and can be missed. Keep other controls in place when an error could have serious consequences.
Maskera supports data minimisation but does not guarantee regulatory compliance. The organisation using the tool remains the data controller.

privacy.metaTitle: privacy policy: local text, cookieless analytics · maskera
privacy.metaDescription: Privacy policy for maskera.dev: text is processed locally in the browser, cookieless web analytics, hosting on Vercel and your rights.
privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.lede: The text you mask is processed locally and is not sent to Maskera. This page describes the limited processing performed by the website itself.

items.title: Data controller
items.body: Hägvall Labs AB (Swedish company reg. no. 559598-0110) is the data controller for maskera.dev. Contact details are available at hagvall-labs.com.

items.title: Web analytics
items.body: Vercel Analytics counts page views using anonymous, cookieless statistics without profiling. The statistics never contain text entered in the tool.

items.title: Hosting
items.body: Vercel may process technical request data, such as IP addresses, to deliver the website and protect it from attacks. The text and restoration key are not included.

items.title: Local setting
items.body: Your light or dark theme choice is saved in the browser's localStorage. It is not a cookie and the value never leaves the device.

items.title: Text entered in the tool
items.body: The text and the key containing the original data are processed locally in the browser. They are not sent to us or any other service for masking.

items.title: Your rights
items.body: Contact us if you have questions about the website's processing or want to exercise your rights.

modes.summary: For clients that accept a custom API URL, such as Claude Code, Codex with an API key and Cursor. The proxy masks what you type and tool results, and restores the reply automatically.

ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8787 claude

modes.label: MCP server
modes.summary: maskera_read_file masks files before the model sees them. maskera_write_file writes the originals back to disk.

modes.label: Guard
modes.summary: Blocks prompts containing personal data in agent hooks and logs only counts and types. With --redact it masks text in a pipe.
modes.code:
# Block PII in agent hooks (exits 2 on match):
npx -y @maskera/mcp guard

# Redact a local file through a pipe:
cat document.txt | npx -y @maskera/mcp guard --redact

about.title: About Maskera
about.lede: Maskera hides Swedish personal data locally before text reaches an AI service, log or analytics.
what: It comes as a browser extension, for AI agents and as an npm package. Everything runs on your device.
about.who: Maskera is developed and operated by Hägvall Labs AB (Swedish company reg. no. 559598-0110), a Swedish limited company in Stockholm founded by Joel Hägvall. The company is the data controller for maskera.dev; how the website itself processes data is described in the privacy policy. The source code, training pipeline and benchmarks are public on GitHub so the results can be reviewed and reproduced.

overview.metaTitle: documentation: local Swedish PII redaction · maskera
overview.metaDescription: Choose the right Maskera mode: browser extension, local LLM proxy, Streamable HTTP or stdio MCP, guard hooks, and npm SDK.
overview.title: Documentation
overview.lede: All masking in Maskera runs locally on your device. Pick the mode that fits where your text lives, set it up in a minute, and verify with made-up data.
overview.verifyBody: npx -y @maskera/mcp doctor reports [ok] for redaction, or the local inspector at http://127.0.0.1:8787/_maskera shows placeholders such as [EPOST_1] going upstream while the reply restores the address.

sections.title: Choose the right mode
sections.body: Maskera offers five entry points backed by the same Swedish rules and local AI model. Pick the one closest to where text is created.

rows: You use web AI chats such as ChatGPT and Claude in the browser.
Every chat prompt and tool output from your AI agent must be masked automatically.
Several clients should share one warm 43 MB AI model, one session vault, and browser approvals.
Your client has no custom API URL and the agent reads and writes local files.
You want to block PII in agent hooks (exit 2) or redact Unix pipes.
You embed Swedish redaction inside your own web app or Node service.

sections.title: 60-second quickstart
sections.body: Use wrap for a single-terminal launch (starts a local proxy, verifies 0 leaks, and prints a session receipt on exit), install a persistent local background service with service install, or configure your MCP client with install for an instant setup receipt.
sections.code:
# 1. Single-terminal launch (injects ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL and OPENAI_BASE_URL)
npx -y @maskera/mcp wrap -- claude

# 2. Or keep the proxy + Streamable HTTP /mcp running in the background (macOS/Linux)
npx -y @maskera/mcp service install --root . --no-raw-restore

# 3. Auto-detect or configure your client + guard hook + setup receipt
npx -y @maskera/mcp install cursor --root . --no-raw-restore --with-hook

sections.title: Let your agent configure Maskera
sections.body: Every page on maskera.dev has a plain Markdown sibling via Accept: text/markdown or a .md suffix (for example /en/docs.md and /en/docs/mcp.md). For a ready-made coding-agent prompt, see /setup-prompt.md and the full index at /llms.txt.
bullets: The MCP server also serves the full workflow skill directly as resource maskera://skills/maskera/SKILL.md and prompt maskera-workflow.
Pass --no-raw-restore when an agent may read and write local files without ever pulling raw PII back into chat.

mcp.metaTitle: @maskera/mcp: proxy, Streamable HTTP, tools and policies · maskera
mcp.metaDescription: Complete reference for @maskera/mcp: all MCP tools, Streamable HTTP /mcp, scoped policy flags, browser approvals, prompts, resources, guard, install, and doctor.
mcp.title: @maskera/mcp reference
mcp.lede: One npm package with seven subcommands: single-command wrap launcher, local LLM proxy with Streamable HTTP /mcp, background service manager, MCP stdio server, hook guard, client installer, and diagnostics.
mcp.verifyBody: Your client lists maskera_list_files, maskera_search_files, maskera_read_file, and maskera_status, and maskera_status reports the active engine mode, roots, and policy.

sections.title: Streamable HTTP (/mcp) and stdio
sections.body: Running maskera-mcp proxy serves both the LLM proxy and a Streamable HTTP MCP endpoint at http://127.0.0.1:8787/mcp. Connected clients share the warm 43 MB ONNX model, the local in-memory session vault, and the live inspector at /_maskera. Clients that only support stdio can launch npx -y @maskera/mcp with no background daemon.
sections.code:
# Warm local service: LLM proxy + Streamable HTTP MCP + live inspector
npx -y @maskera/mcp proxy --root /path/to/workspace

# Tighten policy per MCP connection via query parameters
# http://127.0.0.1:8787/mcp?no_raw_restore=1
# http://127.0.0.1:8787/mcp?read_only=1&no_raw_restore=1
# http://127.0.0.1:8787/mcp?approval_mode=browser

sections.title: MCP tools
sections.body: Every tool declares inputSchema, outputSchema, and MCP annotations (readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, openWorldHint: false).

rows: List regular files inside allowed --root directories without reading contents.
Confined to --root; external symlinks are skipped.
Search local UTF-8 files and redact every matching line before returning. Supports searching by placeholders such as [NAMN_1].
Read a local UTF-8 file (max 2 MiB) and return redacted text + session_id.
Originals stay in local RAM only.
Restore placeholders from session_id and write directly to disk without echoing raw PII into chat.
Hidden in --read-only; requires overwrite: true to replace existing files.
Redact text locally with auto (AI + rules) or rules, profile, and custom_terms.
include_map: true is blocked by --no-raw-restore and gated by approval mode.
Restore placeholders in text from session_id or an explicit map.
Hidden by --no-raw-restore; paused in browser/native approval mode.
List active sessions and entity counts by label.
Erase a session restore map from RAM immediately.
Report model status, cache stats, active sessions, allowed roots, and policy.
Complete a paused approval request after deciding in /_maskera.

sections.title: Scoped policies and approval modes
sections.body: Restrict what each agent connection is allowed to do via CLI flags or /mcp URL query parameters. URL parameters can only tighten server defaults, never weaken them.

rows: Hides and blocks maskera_restore and include_map: true. Agents can still restore files directly to disk with maskera_write_file.
Default for agents working on sensitive files.
Hides and blocks maskera_write_file and maskera_clear_session.
Pauses maskera_restore and include_map: true and shows Approve / Decline controls in http://127.0.0.1:8787/_maskera.
Human confirmation before any raw PII enters chat.
Sends MCP form elicitation (elicitation/create) to the client; fails closed if unsupported.
Clients with native MCP elicitation support.

sections.title: Built-in prompts, resources, and skill
sections.body: The MCP server ships Maskera workflow guidance directly over the protocol so clients need no separate skill install.
bullets: Resource maskera://skills/maskera/SKILL.md serves the complete operating guide as text/markdown.
Resource maskera://status returns live engine, policy, and session status as JSON.
Prompt maskera-workflow accepts optional profile (general or clinical) and custom_terms.
Prompt maskera-redact-file guides a safe read, draft, and local restore file roundtrip.

sections.title: Wrap, service, guard, install, and doctor
sections.body: Alongside proxy and MCP, the CLI includes wrap for a single-terminal launch, service for a local background daemon on macOS (launchd) and Linux (systemd --user), guard for hooks and pipes, install with client auto-detection (--apply, --project, --with-hook) and automatic setup receipts, and doctor for local verification plus a live /mcp probe.
sections.code:
# Start local proxy + verify + launch agent in one terminal
npx -y @maskera/mcp wrap --open -- claude

# Install or check a persistent local background service (127.0.0.1:8787)
npx -y @maskera/mcp service install --root . --no-raw-restore
npx -y @maskera/mcp service status

# Configure client + guard hook + save zero-PII receipt (maskera-setup-receipt/v1)
npx -y @maskera/mcp install claude-code --root . --no-raw-restore --apply --with-hook --receipt ./maskera-receipt.json

# Block PII in hooks (exits 2 on match, prints counts only)
echo '{"prompt":"Ring 070-174 06 58"}' | npx -y @maskera/mcp guard

# Self-test local engine, roots, proxy, and live /mcp
npx -y @maskera/mcp doctor --root . --json

rows: Path-delimited allowed directories for file tools.
auto (AI + rules) or rules (deterministic rules only).
Set to 1 to block raw PII export into model context.
Set to 1 to disable file writes and session clears.
Load a local ONNX model directory completely offline.

clients.metaTitle: client guides: connect Maskera to your AI client · maskera
clients.metaDescription: Step-by-step setup for AI clients such as Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor, with a made-up Swedish data verification test.
clients.title: Client guides
clients.lede: Exact steps and commands per client. Every configuration can also be written or previewed with npx -y @maskera/mcp install <client>.
clients.verifyBody: You send a made-up address (provnamn.maskera@example.com) and see [EPOST_1] in the inspector at http://127.0.0.1:8787/_maskera, or your agent calls maskera_status and returns your allowed roots.

sections.title: Claude Desktop (local proxy)
sections.body: Start the proxy first and leave it running. Choose Help -> Troubleshooting -> Enable Developer Mode, then Developer -> Configure Third-Party Inference. Select third-party inference with Static API key, set base URL http://127.0.0.1:8787 (without /v1), enter your Anthropic API key, and change the auth scheme to x-api-key (Anthropic rejects the default Bearer scheme). Click Apply Changes, then Save & Restart.
bullets: Requests are billed to your Anthropic API key rather than a Claude plan.
While the proxy is stopped, Desktop fails instead of sending unmasked text.
To switch back, pick the Anthropic sign-in option on the sign-in screen.

sections.title: Claude Code (proxy or MCP)
sections.body: With the proxy, every prompt and tool output is masked automatically. For local files over MCP, connect either to the warm Streamable HTTP /mcp endpoint or directly over stdio.
sections.code:
# Proxy (masks full chat + tool outputs)
npx -y @maskera/mcp proxy --root .
ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8787 claude

# Or warm Streamable HTTP MCP blocking raw PII export
claude mcp add --transport http maskera 'http://127.0.0.1:8787/mcp?no_raw_restore=1'

# Or standalone stdio MCP
claude mcp add maskera -- npx -y @maskera/mcp --root . --no-raw-restore

sections.title: Codex (API key or ChatGPT account)
sections.body: With an OpenAI API key, Codex routes straight through the local proxy. If you sign in with a ChatGPT account, Codex requires HTTPS for its base URL, so use the MCP server instead.
sections.code:
# With OpenAI API key (proxy)
npx -y @maskera/mcp proxy --root .
OPENAI_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8787/v1 codex

# Signed in with ChatGPT account (MCP stdio)
codex mcp add maskera -- npx -y @maskera/mcp --root . --no-raw-restore

# Or connect to an already running proxy over Streamable HTTP
codex mcp add maskera --url 'http://127.0.0.1:8787/mcp?no_raw_restore=1'

sections.title: Cursor
sections.body: Run the installer inside your project folder to merge the Maskera entry into .cursor/mcp.json without touching your other servers.
sections.code:
# Write .cursor/mcp.json automatically (stdio)
npx -y @maskera/mcp install cursor --root . --no-raw-restore

# Or connect to a running warm proxy (/mcp)
npx -y @maskera/mcp install cursor --transport http --no-raw-restore

sections.title: OpenCode and T3 Code
sections.body: Both OpenCode (opencode.json under mcp.servers) and T3 Code support stdio and Streamable HTTP through the same installer.
sections.code:
# OpenCode (merges into opencode.json)
npx -y @maskera/mcp install opencode --root . --no-raw-restore

# T3 Code (prints ready-to-paste JSON)
npx -y @maskera/mcp install t3-code --root . --no-raw-restore

sections.title: Test with made-up data
sections.body: Always run a quick check before handling real personal data. The inspector keeps everything in local RAM and hides original values until you click reveal.
sections.code:
# Run automated diagnostics
npx -y @maskera/mcp doctor --root .

# Open local live inspector and approvals view
open http://127.0.0.1:8787/_maskera

sdk.metaTitle: SDK & operations: maskera, @maskera/core and self-hosting · maskera
sdk.metaDescription: Embed Swedish PII redaction in browsers and Node.js with maskera and @maskera/core: clinical profile, custom rules, ONNX self-hosting, and production checklist.
sdk.title: SDK and operations
sdk.lede: Use maskera (rules + 43 MB Swedish AI model) or @maskera/core (rules only, zero dependencies) directly in your own TypeScript or JavaScript code.
sdk.verifyBody: redactWithNer replaces names, personnummer, and places with placeholders locally in your process and restore(answer) brings back the exact originals without the key leaving your device.

sections.title: Pick a package
sections.body: Both packages share the same synchronous rule engine and restore map. maskera re-exports everything from @maskera/core.

rows: Deterministic Swedish rules + 43 MB q4/q8 ONNX model (maskera-sv-ner).
Free-form Swedish text with names, street addresses, places, and organisations.
Format and check-digit rules only, zero dependencies, synchronous.
Structured logs, constrained runtimes, or when you want no model weights.

sections.title: Core flow, clinical profile, and custom detectors
sections.body: Create one recognizer at startup and reuse it across calls. For Swedish healthcare text, profile: "clinical" retains doses, measurements, and care terms while masking personal data. Add custom patterns with regexDetector.

sections.title: Self-hosting the model and offline operation
sections.body: By default, model weights (sha256-verified against a pinned commit) are fetched once from Hugging Face and cached locally. For air-gapped networks or internal servers, host the folder locally and disable remote fetches.

sections.title: Production checklist
sections.body: Maskera is defense in depth, not a zero-leak compliance guarantee. Follow four operational rules:
bullets: Reuse one createNerRecognizer() instance per process so the model is not reloaded per request.
Never store the restore map in the same log, database, or trace as the redacted text.
Fail closed on model errors: never fall through and forward unredacted text if NER throws.
Run a synthetic smoke test on deploy with made-up Swedish data before sending real traffic.

troubleshooting.metaDescription: Resolve common issues with @maskera/mcp and maskera: 502 fail-closed, Codex with ChatGPT login, offline models, loopback protection, and known boundaries.
troubleshooting.title: Troubleshooting and boundaries
troubleshooting.lede: Common issues, why Maskera blocks rather than silently forwarding unredacted text, and where local masking stops.
troubleshooting.verifyBody: Run npx -y @maskera/mcp doctor --root . to see which layer failed (Node version, directory access, ONNX model, or local proxy).

sections.title: Common errors and fixes
sections.body: Every security-critical mode in @maskera/mcp fails closed so raw text is never forwarded silently.

rows: Local NER failed to run or the upstream API is unreachable.
Check stderr or run doctor. If you only want deterministic rules, pass --rules-only.
Codex with ChatGPT login rejects http://127.0.0.1:8787
ChatGPT sign-in requires HTTPS for a custom base URL.
Use the MCP server (codex mcp add maskera -- npx -y @maskera/mcp --root .) instead of the proxy.
Auth scheme is still set to Bearer.
Switch auth scheme to x-api-key and verify base URL is http://127.0.0.1:8787 without /v1.
Host or Origin header does not match the loopback listener.
Always open http://127.0.0.1:8787/_maskera directly and call /mcp without a foreign Origin header.
The path or a symlink points outside --root.
Start with the right --root <dir> (repeatable for multiple folders).
This is intentional protection. Use maskera_write_file to restore directly to disk, or --approval-mode browser.

sections.title: Running completely offline
sections.body: When your workstation or server cannot reach Hugging Face, place the model directory on local disk and disable remote fetches.

sections.title: Security boundaries
sections.body: Be clear internally about what local masking covers and what it does not replace:
bullets: Maskera is built for Swedish (and mixed Swedish/English) text. Other languages are only partially covered.
Images and scanned PDFs must be converted to text via OCR before passing through Maskera.
A neural model can miss unusual names or typos (see measured numbers on /en/accuracy). Add known client names and case IDs via --custom-term.
A skill guides agent behaviour but can be bypassed if the agent has unrestricted shell tools. Hard enforcement requires the local proxy or restricting file access to Maskera MCP.
